summary: Studied envh client post-run termination logic (client/commands.py: spawn, processes_with_marker, terminate_lingering, marker env-injection, signal/exit-code handling), run AS redteam/redteam2. Found NO flag exfil, NO cross-user kill, NO approval/marker subversion. The run-marker cleanup is sound precisely because /proc/<pid>/environ is uid-restricted (0400) and the marker is a 128-bit CSPRNG value injected only into the spawned child. One LOW client-robustness gap (uncaught PermissionError on a pid-reuse TOCTOU) causes attacker-self-harm only; REJECTED as a charter win.

candidates.title: terminate_lingering() catches only ProcessLookupError; an os.kill EPERM from a pid-reuse TOCTOU propagates uncaught and crashes the attacker's own client
repro_cmds: # As redteam2, create a cross-user stand-in pid (simulates a pid reused by another uid between enumerate and kill):
sudo -u redteam2 env ENVH_RUN_MARKER=x sh -c 'echo $$ > /tmp/rt2.pid; chmod 644 /tmp/rt2.pid; exec sleep 120' &
# As redteam, force that pid into the kill list and call the client's own terminate_lingering:
sudo -u redteam /opt/ctf/venv/bin/python -c "import sys,envh.client.commands as c; c.processes_with_marker=lambda m:[int(sys.argv[1])]; c.terminate_lingering('m')" $VPID
candidates.observed_output: PermissionError(1, 'Operation not permitted') propagates out of terminate_lingering uncaught (the function wraps os.kill only in `except ProcessLookupError`, commands.py lines 106-109 and 113-117). The cross-user victim is NOT signalled (EPERM blocks delivery) and stays alive; only the attacker's own client process would crash.
candidates.why_novel: F7 was untouched in Wave 1; this exception-handling gap is not mentioned in README/SECURITY.md. However it has no cross-user/broker/flag impact.
candidates.notes: Not a charter win: (1) requires an unreliable pid-reuse race (pid enumerated by processes_with_marker exits and is reused before os.kill, ~<2.1s window); (2) EPERM means no other user's process is actually signalled, so no cross-user harm; (3) worst case is the attacker's OWN client crashing or mis-signalling the attacker's OWN unrelated same-uid process (self-harm); (4) the broker is never involved. A hardening fix would also catch PermissionError. Recorded so later waves don't re-chase it as a cross-user primitive.

negative_results: CROSS-USER KILL IS BLOCKED (primary result, proven). redteam2 runs `sleep 300` carrying ENVH_RUN_MARKER=CROSSMARKER_511bd34b3c4809f3. /proc/<pid>/environ of that process is mode -r-------- owned by redteam2. As redteam: direct read of /proc/<pid>/environ -> PermissionError [Errno 13]; client's processes_with_marker(marker) -> [] (victim NOT in list); os.kill(pid,0) -> PermissionError [Errno 1] EPERM. So envh's run cleanup can NEVER enumerate or kill another user's process: the environ-match gate is itself the uid boundary.

MARKER NOT GUESSABLE/FORCEABLE. Marker is secrets.token_hex(16) = 128-bit CSPRNG, generated fresh per run in cmd_run (line 54). No cross-run reuse, never printed, never sent over the socket. Cannot be brute-forced or predicted to pre-mark a victim.

PRE-SET ENVH_RUN_MARKER CANNOT SUBVERT TERMINATION (proven). Ran `sudo -u redteam env ENVH_RUN_MARKER=ATTACKER_CHOSEN_VALUE python ...` reproducing cmd_run's exact env merge `{**os.environ, RUN_MARKER_VAR: fresh}` (line 55): the child receives the FRESH random marker (attacker's pre-set value is overridden because extra_env is applied last); terminate_lingering(fresh) does NOT touch a victim pre-marked with the attacker-chosen value (victim stayed alive). Pre-setting the var has zero effect on which pids are killed.

CLIENT/SHELL DO NOT SELF-MATCH (proven). The fresh marker is placed only in the spawned child's environ, never in the client's own os.environ (verified: client's own /proc/self/environ does not contain the marker) and processes_with_marker excludes os.getpid(). The parent shell is unreadable anyway (it is the setuid-root `sudo` wrapper -> PermissionError). So `envh run` cannot kill its own client, its parent shell, or any ancestor via the marker.

SAME-USER CLEANUP WORKS AS INTENDED (control, not a vuln). As redteam, spawning an own child with the marker then calling terminate_lingering kills exactly that child (SIGTERM, returncode -15). This is the designed behavior (an attacker terminating only its own same-uid processes is no privilege gain, since it can already kill them directly). Not a finding.

EXIT-CODE MATH IS CORRECT. spawn() returns `128 - returncode` when returncode<0 (signal death) = 128+signum (e.g. SIGKILL->137, SIGTERM->143), else the raw exit status; standard shell convention, no off-by-one, no overflow (Popen exit codes 0-255).

SIGNAL FORWARDING HAS NO SECURITY IMPACT. Client ignores SIGINT, forwards SIGTERM/SIGHUP to the child; child.send_signal wrapped in `except ProcessLookupError`. No way to redirect a signal to a non-child process.

--keep-background leaving values in surviving processes is explicitly documented in the client help ('do not terminate processes the command leaves running (they keep the values)') and matches README's acknowledged same-user value exposure; not novel.
out_of_scope_observations: processes_with_marker reads every readable /proc/<pid>/environ and terminate_lingering re-scans up to ~42 times (2s / 0.05s) per run; this is attacker-self-cost on the attacker's own client only, never touches the broker, so it is not a broker DoS and is out of scope for a charter win.
The only way the F7 marker scan could ever read another user's process environ is as root (ptrace_may_access bypass) -- out of scope per CHARTER 3.3 (reading another uid's /proc/<pid>/environ).
